formulations.label: Solution for injection in single-dose pre-filled pen (once weekly)
formulations.strengths: 0.75 mg, 1.5 mg, 3 mg, 4.5 mg (each in 0.5 mL)

src.q: Each pre-filled pen contains 1.5 mg of dulaglutide* in 0.5 ml solution.
Each pre-filled pen contains 4.5 mg of dulaglutide* in 0.5 ml solution.
Each pre-filled pen contains 0.75 mg of dulaglutide* in 0.5 ml solution.
Each pre-filled pen contains 3 mg of dulaglutide* in 0.5 ml solution.

brandPrescribing.t: SPS: dulaglutide is a biological medicine and must be prescribed and dispensed by brand name. The SmPC also asks that the product name and batch number be recorded (traceability).

src.q: Biological medicines such as semaglutide, dulaglutide, liraglutide, and tirzepatide must be prescribed and dispensed by brand name.
In order to improve the traceability of biological medicinal products, the name and the batch number of the administered medicinal product should be clearly recorded.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes in patients aged 10 years and above, with diet and exercise: monotherapy when metformin is inappropriate (intolerance or contraindication), or added to other diabetes medicines.

src.q: indicated for the treatment of patients 10 years and above with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus as an adjunct to diet and exercise
as monotherapy when metformin is considered inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications in addition to other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes

items.t: SPS: prescribe and dispense by brand name (biological medicine). Only prescribe for licensed indications.

src.q: Biological medicines such as semaglutide, dulaglutide, liraglutide, and tirzepatide must be prescribed and dispensed by brand name.
Only prescribe GLP-1 RAs, or incretin mimetics, for their licensed indication and follow NHS guidance.

items.t: Monotherapy: 0.75 mg once weekly.

src.q: Monotherapy The recommended dose is 0.75 mg once weekly.

items.t: Add-on therapy: 1.5 mg once weekly. If needed, increase after at least 4 weeks to 3 mg, then after at least 4 more weeks to 4.5 mg. Maximum 4.5 mg once weekly.

src.q: Add-on therapy The recommended dose is 1.5 mg once weekly.

If needed, the 1.5 mg dose can be increased after at least 4 weeks to 3 mg once weekly. the 3 mg dose can be increased after at least 4 weeks to 4.5 mg once weekly. The maximum dose is 4.5 mg once weekly.

items.t: With metformin, pioglitazone or an SGLT2 inhibitor: continue their current dose. With a sulphonylurea or insulin: a dose reduction of these may be considered; reduce insulin stepwise with blood glucose self-monitoring.

src.q: When it is added to existing therapy of a sulphonylurea or insulin, a reduction in the dose of sulphonylurea or insulin may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia
A stepwise approach to insulin dose reduction is recommended.

items.t: Missed dose: give as soon as possible if at least 3 days (72 hours) remain before the next dose; otherwise skip it and give the next dose on the usual day.

src.q: If a dose is missed, it should be administered as soon as possible if there are at least 3 days (72 hours) until the next scheduled dose.
If less than 3 days (72 hours) remain before the next scheduled dose, the missed dose should be skipped and the next dose should be administered on the regularly scheduled day.

items.t: Elderly and hepatic impairment: no dose adjustment.

src.q: Elderly No dose adjustment is required based on age
No dose adjustment is required in patients with hepatic impairment.

items.t: Children 10 years and above: start 0.75 mg once weekly; if needed increase to 1.5 mg once weekly after at least 4 weeks. Maximum 1.5 mg once weekly. Not established under 10 years (no data).

src.q: The starting dose for paediatric patients 10 years and above is 0.75 mg once weekly. If needed, the dose can be increased to 1.5 mg once weekly after at least 4 weeks. The maximum dose is 1.5 mg once weekly.
The safety and efficacy of dulaglutide in children aged less than 10 years have not been established and no data are available

items.t: Hypersensitivity to dulaglutide or any excipient.

src.q: Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Should not be used in type 1 diabetes or to treat diabetic ketoacidosis; not a substitute for insulin. Diabetic ketoacidosis reported after rapid stopping or reduction of insulin.

src.q: Dulaglutide should not be used in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus or for the treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Dulaglutide is not a substitute for insulin.
Diabetic ketoacidosis has been reported in insulin-dependent patients after rapid discontinuation or dose reduction of insulin

items.t: Severe gastrointestinal disease, including severe gastroparesis: not studied; not recommended. Monitor and consider dose change or stopping if severe gastrointestinal symptoms develop.

src.q: Dulaglutide has not been studied in patients with severe gastrointestinal disease, including severe gastroparesis, and is therefore not recommended in these patients.
Monitor and consider dose modification or discontinuation in patients who develop severe gastrointestinal symptoms while on treatment.

items.t: General anaesthesia or deep sedation: pulmonary aspiration reported with GLP-1 receptor agonists (delayed gastric emptying); consider before procedures.

src.q: the increased risk of residual gastric content due to delayed gastric emptying (see section 4.8) should be considered prior to performing procedures with general anaesthesia or deep sedation

items.t: Dehydration, sometimes causing acute renal failure or worse renal impairment, especially at the start: warn patients and advise them to avoid fluid loss.

src.q: Dehydration, sometimes leading to acute renal failure or worsening renal impairment, has been reported in patients treated with dulaglutide, especially at the initiation of treatment.
take precautions to avoid fluid depletion

items.t: Acute pancreatitis (including necrotising and fatal cases): caution with a history of pancreatitis (not studied). Stop if suspected; do not restart if confirmed.

src.q: Dulaglutide has not been studied in patients with a history of pancreatitis, and should be used with caution in these patients.
If pancreatitis is suspected, dulaglutide should be discontinued. If the diagnosis of pancreatitis is confirmed, dulaglutide should not be restarted.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia with a sulphonylurea or insulin: may be lowered by reducing their dose.

src.q: The risk of hypoglycaemia may be lowered by a reduction in the dose of sulphonylurea or insulin

items.t: Sulphonylureas or insulin: hypoglycaemia; a dose reduction may be considered. MHRA: diabetic ketoacidosis reported when insulin was rapidly reduced or stopped; reduce insulin stepwise with glucose self-monitoring.

src.q: Patients receiving dulaglutide in combination with sulphonylurea or insulin may have an increased risk of hypoglycaemia.
if the insulin dose is to be reduced, a stepwise approach is recommended

items.t: Sitagliptin: increases dulaglutide exposure, which may enhance its blood-glucose effect.

src.q: Dulaglutide (1.5 mg) coadministration with sitagliptin increased dulaglutide exposure and Cmax by approximately 38 % and 27 %, respectively
The increased exposure may enhance the effects of dulaglutide on blood glucose levels.

items.t: Oral medicines with rapid absorption or prolonged release: delayed gastric emptying may alter exposure, particularly when starting dulaglutide. Studied medicines (paracetamol, atorvastatin, digoxin, lisinopril, metoprolol, warfarin, oral contraceptives, metformin) need no dose adjustment.

src.q: For patients receiving dulaglutide in combination with oral medicinal products with rapid gastrointestinal absorption or prolonged release, there is a potential for altered medicinal product exposure, particularly at the time of dulaglutide treatment initiation.
No dose adjustment for warfarin is necessary when given together with dulaglutide.
No dose adjustment of paracetamol is necessary when administered with dulaglutide.

items.t: SPS: use with caution with time-critical or narrow therapeutic window medicines (e.g. levodopa); extra monitoring may be needed.

src.q: Use GLP-1 RAs with caution in people who are taking medicines which are time critical, such as levodopa for Parkinson's disease.
These people may require additional monitoring.

items.t: eGFR < 90 to ≥ 15 mL/min/1.73 m²: no dose adjustment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required in patients with mild, moderate or severe renal impairment (eGFR < 90 to ≥ 15 mL/min/1.73m2).

items.t: End-stage renal disease (eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73 m²): very limited experience; cannot be recommended.

src.q: There is very limited experience in patients with end stage renal disease (< 15 ml/min/1.73m2), therefore Trulicity cannot be recommended in this population

items.t: Dehydration from gastrointestinal effects can cause acute renal failure or worsen renal impairment.

src.q: Many of the reported adverse renal events occurred in patients who had experienced nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, or dehydration.

items.t: No dose adjustment in hepatic impairment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required in patients with hepatic impairment.

items.t: SmPC: no or limited human data; animal reproductive toxicity. Not recommended in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no or limited amount of data from the use of dulaglutide in pregnant women.
Therefore, the use of dulaglutide is not recommended during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: GLP-1 receptor agonists should not be used in pregnancy. If used by accident in early pregnancy, available data (about 47,000 pregnancies) are reassuring; no extra monitoring for birth defects is needed.

src.q: GLP-1 receptor agonists should not be used in pregnancy.
If you accidentally used a GLP-1 receptor agonist in early pregnancy, you can be reassured that the available information suggests that it does not harm the baby.
No extra monitoring for major birth defects is required following use in early pregnancy of a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

items.t: SmPC: unknown if excreted in human milk; a risk to the infant cannot be excluded. Should not be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: A risk to newborns/infants cannot be excluded.
Dulaglutide should not be used during breast-feeding.

items.t: SPS: MHRA advise GLP-1 receptor agonists should not be taken while breastfeeding (lack of safety data). Insulin or metformin are preferred choices.

src.q: The MHRA advise GLP-1 RAs should not be taken by people who are breastfeeding due to a lack of safety data .
Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.

items.t: SPS: MHRA advise contraception throughout GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment as a precaution. Dulaglutide did not affect oral contraceptive exposure (no dose change needed).

src.q: They advise contraceptive use throughout GLP-1 RA treatment as a cautionary measure.
No dose adjustment for oral contraceptives is required when given together with dulaglutide.

items.t: Fertility: effect in humans unknown; no direct effect in rats.

src.q: The effect of dulaglutide on fertility in humans is unknown.

items.t: Most frequent: nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea, usually mild or moderate and short-lived; they peak in the first 2 weeks. Up to 104 weeks at 1.5 mg: nausea 21.2%, diarrhoea 13.7%, vomiting 11.5%.

src.q: The most frequently reported adverse reactions in clinical trials were gastrointestinal, including nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea.
nausea (12.9 % and 21.2 % ) , diarrhoea (10.7 % and 13.7 %) and vomiting (6.9 % and 11.5 %)
reported to peak during the first 2 weeks of treatment

items.t: Hypoglycaemia: documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia in about 40% with a sulphonylurea plus metformin and 35.3% with insulin glargine (1.5 mg); 5.9% to 10.9% with monotherapy or metformin (with or without pioglitazone).

src.q: the incidences of documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia were 5.9 % to 10.9 %
were used in combination with a sulphonylurea and metformin were 39.0 % and 40.3 %
The incidence of documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia when dulaglutide 1.5 mg was used in combination with insulin glargine was 35.3 %

items.t: Small heart rate rise (2 to 4 beats per minute), sinus tachycardia, first-degree AV block; injection site reactions.

src.q: Small mean increases in heart rate of 2 to 4 beats per minute (bpm)
Injection site adverse events were reported in 1.9 % of patients receiving dulaglutide.

items.t: Acute pancreatitis, including necrotising and fatal cases: persistent, severe abdominal pain. Stop if suspected; do not restart if confirmed. Patients should seek urgent medical attention.

src.q: This includes post-marketing reports of necrotising pancreatitis and reports with a fatal outcome.
if pancreatitis is suspected, discontinue treatment with the GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist immediately; do not restart therapy if the diagnosis of pancreatitis is confirmed

items.t: Dehydration leading to acute renal failure or worsening renal impairment.

src.q: Dehydration, sometimes leading to acute renal failure or worsening renal impairment, has been reported in patients treated with dulaglutide

items.t: Anaphylactic reaction and angioedema (post-marketing); severe gastroparesis; non-mechanical intestinal obstruction; cholelithiasis and cholecystitis.

src.q: Cases of anaphylactic reaction have been rarely reported with marketed use of dulaglutide.
Events related to impaired gastric emptying, including severe gastroparesis, have been reported.
Non-mechanical intestinal obstruction Hepatobiliary disorders Cholelithiasis, cholecystitis

items.t: Blood glucose self-monitoring is not needed for dulaglutide itself, but is needed to adjust sulphonylurea or insulin doses, especially at the start.

src.q: The use of Trulicity does not require blood glucose self-monitoring.
Blood glucose self-monitoring is necessary to adjust the dose of sulphonylurea or insulin, particularly when Trulicity therapy is started and insulin is reduced.

items.t: Watch for severe gastrointestinal symptoms; consider dose change or stopping.

src.q: Monitor and consider dose modification or discontinuation in patients who develop severe gastrointestinal symptoms while on treatment.

items.t: Stop if pancreatitis is suspected; do not restart if confirmed. Raised pancreatic enzymes alone do not predict pancreatitis.

src.q: If pancreatitis is suspected, dulaglutide should be discontinued.
elevations in pancreatic enzymes alone are not predictive of acute pancreatitis

items.t: Subcutaneous injection once weekly into the abdomen, thigh or upper arm, at any time of day, with or without meals. Never intravenous or intramuscular.

src.q: Trulicity is to be injected subcutaneously in the abdomen, thigh or upper arm. It should not be administered intravenously or intramuscularly.
The dose can be administered at any time of day, with or without meals.

items.t: The weekly injection day can be changed if the last dose was at least 3 days (72 hours) before.

src.q: The day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary, as long as the last dose was administered 3 or more days (72 hours) before.

items.t: Seek urgent medical help for severe, persistent abdominal pain that may go through to the back, with or without nausea and vomiting (possible pancreatitis).

src.q: seek urgent medical attention if you experience severe, persistent abdominal pain, that may radiate to your back and may be accompanied by nausea and vomiting

items.t: Drink plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration, especially if you have vomiting or diarrhoea.

src.q: throughout treatment stay well hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids (such as water) to avoid dehydration

items.t: Tell your healthcare team and anaesthetist before any surgery or sedation that you use this medicine; do not stop it without discussing with your doctor.

src.q: make sure you inform your healthcare team including the anaesthetist about this prior to your surgical procedure
take your prescribed medicine(s) as usual and do not stop your treatment without first discussing this with your doctor

items.t: If you also use insulin: learn the signs of diabetic ketoacidosis and get urgent help if they occur.

src.q: Inform patients of the signs and symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, excessive thirst, increased frequency of urination, difficulty breathing, confusion, unusual fatigue, or sleepiness)

items.t: With a sulphonylurea or insulin, take precautions to avoid low blood sugar while driving.

src.q: patients should be advised to take precautions to avoid hypoglycaemia while driving and using machines
